OBJECTIVES
Karnaugh maps provide a systematic method for simplifying Boolean equations.
WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ +WXYZ +WXYZ +
INTRODUCTIONM
Just think of trying to simplify this four variable eleven term equation using the properties, rules and theorems!
Simplifying using the properties, rules and theorems requires knowing them well and often requires cleverness.
On the other hand, Karnaugh maps provide a cookbook approach for simplifying equations.
In this lesson you will learn about KARNAUGH MAPS.INFINITY................
LESSON MENU
DEVELOPING KARNAUGH MAPS
The Karnaugh map is composed of an arrangement of adjacent cells.
DISCUSSION
Each cell represents one particular combination of variables.
In the case of two variables, four cells are required to produce the four combinations.
To use the Karnaugh map, the terms are written outside the cells.
The variables to the left of the cells applies to each cell in that row.
The variables above the cells applies to each cell in that column.
As you can see, each cell represents a combination of the two variables X,Y.
What is each block called in a Karnaugh map?
A term is a combination of variables such as XY, XY, XY or XY.

To use Karnaugh maps, the Boolean equation must be in the sum of products form.
The equation XY + XY is in the sum of products form and can be placed in a Karnaugh map.
Take the first term and place a 1 in the appropriate cell of the map. A 1 goes into the XY cell, lower right hand corner.
Continue with the next term. A 1 is placed in the XY cell, lower left hand corner.
Since there are only two terms, the map is complete.

You know that the equations can contain more than two variables.
Let's see how three and four variable Karnaugh maps are constructed.
The three variable map uses two variables to form rows and one variable to form columns, eight cells.
Note, that the cells are arranged such that there is only a single variable change between rows.
This is very important and must be done so that Boolean equations are simplified correctly!
Filling in the map uses the same procedure as a two variable map.
XYZ + XYZ + XYZ + XYZ
Again, you can develop a Karnaugh map directly from a truth table.
Now, try filling in a Karnaugh map on your own. Use paper and pencil to draw the map, and then fill it in.
WXZ + WXZ + WXZ
The four variable map uses two variables to form rows and two variables to form columns, sixteen cells.
Note, that the cells are arranged such that there is only a single variable change between rows and columns.
Again, this is very important and must be done so that Boolean equations are simplified correctly!
Filling in the map uses the same procedure as a two or three variable map.
WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ
Again, you can develop a Karnaugh map directly from a truth table.
W X Y Z F(X,Y,Z))

SIMPLIFYING USING KARNAUGH MAPS
Once a Boolean equation is mapped, it can be simplified. APHICS TEXT: WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ
WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ +WXYZ +WXYZ +
DISCUSSION
Use adjacent cells, adjacent cells differ by only a single variable.
The 1's in adjacent cells are combined in groups of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, etc...
Each group of 1's is maximized to include the largest number of adjacent cells.
Every 1 on the map must be in a group of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, etc. Overlapping groups are OK.
Each group represents a simplified product by eliminating opposite terms in each group and then the products are summed. TEXT: WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ = WXZ + XYZ + WXYZ (YY) (WW)
WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ + WXYZ = WXZ + XYZ + WXYZ

Now, let's simplify using Karnaugh maps....................
There is one group of adjacent 1's. The grouping is maximized and all 1's are in a group.
Simplifying Y is eliminated because both Y and Y variables are in the group.
Only X remains because X is not in the group.
So, the Karnaugh map simplified the XY + XY equation to X.

To maximize the process, place all 1's in as few groups as possible..
